title: A related good's price changes

readouts.l: Rival console B: P and Q

predict.q: The price of games consoles falls by 20%. What happens to the market for console games?

options.s: Demand shifts right: more games are demanded at every price.
options.fb: Consoles and games are complements (XED −1.5): a 20% cut in console prices raises demand for games by 30% at every price.

options.s: Demand shifts left: buyers spend their money on consoles instead.
options.fb: Cheaper consoles mean more consoles bought, and every console needs games: complements.

options.s: A movement down the demand curve for games.
options.fb: The price of games has not changed first; the change in a related good's price shifts demand for games.
Console prices affect buyers of games, so demand shifts, not supply.

task: Move the console-price slider (try both directions) and watch demand for games and for a substitute console.

target.do: Move the console-price slider to −20%, then press Check.

takeaway: A change in a related good's price shifts demand. Complements move the opposite way to the price; substitutes move the same way.
